items.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: Joe Wilder — I was working with Joe Wilder at that time, and Wayne Andre and Jimmy Maxwell. And so we reconstructed the thing

ctx.x: Well I’ll tell you, I’ve always loved musicians’ stories, and it’s been one of the nicest things about hanging out with musicians is that they remember even adversity in humorous terms after the original pain is over. And I used to love to sit around and listen to Roy Eldridge tell stories, and Hot Lips Page and people like that. It would just knock me out that there was such a slice of life there, and usually it was a funny story about somebody else. You know you could rag on somebody to tell about their foibles…

material. I’ve been doing it for something like twelve years now. And I still every time I put together my month’s column I look and I see that I still have enough for another column in my computer, and by the time I get around to the next month I’ve gathered enough other things that I’ve still, I’ve never had to reach back or hurry and interview somebody. It’s just been a natural thing. So well I really got started writing again in the 80s there someplace. I knew Gene Lees who had been the editor of Down Beat…

anecdotes collection. And he asked his writers, who would you recommend to edit this. And they both pointed at me.
